Title: Diagnosis of test `testOptionComparatorInsertedOrder`

Details: The test `testOptionComparatorInsertedOrder` checks whether the order of `Option` objects returned by `getOptions().getOptions()` matches the expected `insertedOrder`. The source code for `getOptions()` shows that `Options` object is created and several `Option` instances are added, including some added via option groups.

Investigating how the underlying collection of options is maintained, `Options.getOptions()` returns an unmodifiable collection backed by `helpOptions()`, which returns a List constructed from the values of the `shortOpts` map. The `shortOpts` map is declared as a `LinkedHashMap`, which normally preserves insertion order.

When adding an option via `Options.addOption(Option)`, the option is put into `shortOpts` with `shortOpts.put(key, opt)`. Since `shortOpts` is a `LinkedHashMap`, the order of insertion should be preserved.

However, options added via `addOptionGroup` (called by `buildOptionsGroup`) do not seem to be individually added to `shortOpts`. The `buildOptionsGroup` method only adds groups to the `Options` object but does not individually add each option to `shortOpts`.

Therefore, the options inside groups might be excluded or ordered differently from those added directly. This could cause the iterator returned by `getOptions()` to not match `insertedOrder`.

Hence, the root cause of the failed test is that options added via option groups are not individually added to the underlying `shortOpts` map, causing order discrepancies and possible omissions when retrieving the options collection.

Recommended fixes should ensure that options inside groups are individually added to `shortOpts` (or ordered properly) so that `getOptions()` returns options in the correct inserted order.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.cli.Options.addOption(org.apache.commons.cli.Option)
org.apache.commons.cli.Options.addOptionGroup(org.apache.commons.cli.OptionGroup)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
